extracted.intended_audience: general readers seeking guidance on personal civility and table manners (learners of historical etiquette)
extracted.subtask_description: A compact set of rules governing polite speech, behavior, and especially table manners — instructing how to converse, dine, and comport oneself in company. Includes prescriptions for speaking of religion, honoring parents, and preserving good humor and conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: 88th. Be not tedious in Discourse, make not many Digressions, nor repeat often the Same manner of Discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid long prefaces, excessive apologies or ceremonious circumlocution; enter promptly on the subject and continue to the end without hesitation. Be concise; avoid digressions and frequent repetition of the same expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of anti-patterns: lengthy prefaces like 'Pardon me Sir if I do not know how to express myself sufficiently well' and other tedious ceremonies. Advice: begin with moderate boldness and proceed steadily to the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 89th. Speak not Evil of the absent for it is unjust
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not criticize, detract from, or slander people who are not present; it is unjust to besmirch a good name in their absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: absent persons cannot defend themselves or clear their name; avoid making accusations or condemning remarks about them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90th. Being Set at meat Scratch not neither Spit Cough or blow your Nose except there's a Necessity for it
rubrics_metrics.description: When seated at table avoid scratching, spitting, coughing, or blowing your nose; if absolutely necessary do so discreetly and with as little noise as possible, turning your face aside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Washington's MS omitted grace-before-meal passages; nevertheless the rule prescribes discretion and minimal disturbance when bodily needs arise at table.

rubrics_metrics.name: 91st. Make no Shew of taking great Delight in your Victuals; Feed not with Greediness; cut your Bread with a Knife, lean not on the Table neither find fault with what you Eat
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not eat like a glutton or make an ostentatious display of delight; cut bread with a knife (unless small fresh roll and others use hands); do not lean on the table or rest shoulders/arms unbecomingly; answer host about food preferences modestly and tactfully; do not complain of dishes or demand alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Custom note: At Washington's table guests were invited to call for preferred wine. Anti-patterns: showing excessive pleasure, complaining about meals, or making demands of host.

rubrics_metrics.name: 92d. Take no Salt or cut Bread with your Knife Greasy
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking salt be careful your knife is not greasy; if necessary clean knife or fork discreetly on a piece of bread or (in some places) with the napkin, but never wipe it on the whole loaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: maintain cleanliness when handling condiments; do not soil common bread.

rubrics_metrics.name: 93d. Entertaining any one at table it is decent to present him w't meat; Undertake not to help others undesired by y'e Master
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are entertaining, it is polite to serve guests and present dishes to them; if you are a guest, wait to be served by the host rather than helping yourself, unless the host invites you or you are at home. Avoid being officious in someone else's house unless circumstances (many guests, host unable to attend) make it necessary to help those nearest you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes duties when hosting vs. visiting; guidance about appropriate deference to host's authority and when assisting is permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 94th. If you Soak bread in the Sauce let it be no more than what you put in your Mouth at a time and blow not your broth at Table but Stay till Cools of it Self
rubrics_metrics.description: If dipping bread or meat into sauce, do not dip immediately after biting; dip only a moderately-sized morsel that can be eaten in one mouthful. Do not blow on food; let hot dishes cool naturally or stir soup gently with a spoon; do not drink up soup at table but use a spoon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns: repeated dipping after biting, blowing on viands, slurping soup. Practical: cool soup by gentle stirring, take soup with a spoon.

rubrics_metrics.name: 95th. Put not your meat to your Mouth with your Knife in your hand; neither Spit forth the Stones of any fruit Pye upon a Dish nor cast anything under the table
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not carry food to your mouth while still holding the knife like a rustic. Do not spit cores (e.g., cherry, plum stones) onto the serving dish; collect them decently (left hand near mouth) and place on edge of your plate. Do not throw bones, peelings, wine, or similar things under the table or on the floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both manners of handling utensils and disposal of refuse; advises decency and containment of waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: 96th. It's unbecoming to Stoop much to one's Meat; Keep your Fingers clean & when foul wipe them on a Corner of your Table Napkin
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid bending excessively over your bowl or plate; bend only slightly when conveying food to avoid soiling yourself, then straighten up. Do not clean hands on the whole loaf; if very greasy, clean on a small piece of bread then on your napkin to avoid soiling it. Do not lick or noisily suck your fingers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages correct posture and discreet cleaning. Suggests that proper use of spoon and fork reduces need to soil napkin.

rubrics_metrics.name: 97th. Put not another bit into your Mouth till the former be Swallowed; let not your Morsels be too big for the jowls
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not take another morsel until the previous one is swallowed; morsels should be moderate so as not to overfill the jaws; usually use the right hand and not both hands to raise food to the mouth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical injunction about portion size and timing between bites; hand etiquette (use right hand).

rubrics_metrics.name: 98th. Drink not nor talk with your mouth full neither Gaze about you While you are a Drinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not drink while you have food in your mouth; do not ask for or talk while drinking; do not drink merely because your neighbor or the head of the table drinks; while drinking, do not gaze around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Side note: later French book recommends keeping eyes 'fixed at the bottom of the glass' while drinking. Emphasizes restraint and attention while drinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: 99th. Drink not too leisurely nor yet too hastily. Before and after Drinking wipe your Lips; breath not then or Ever with too Great a Noise, for its uncivil
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not drink too slowly (or too hastily like gulping) nor too frequently nor without water. Wipe your lips before and after drinking and avoid breathing loudly at any time, which is inelegant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames drinking pace as a matter of decorum; cautions against drunkard-like behavior and noisy breathing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 100th. Cleanse not your teeth with the Table Cloth Napkin Fork or Knife but if Others do it let it be done w't a Pick Tooth
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not clean your teeth using the tablecloth, napkin, finger, fork, or knife; using nails is worse. Use a toothpick. It is generally inappropriate to pick teeth at table unless others do so and it is the custom among the more civilized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable implement (toothpick) and social exception (custom of company).

rubrics_metrics.name: 101st. Rince not your Mouth in the Presence of Others
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rinse your mouth with wine or otherwise spit/reject it in the presence of others; when opportunities to wash are offered (even at table), wash only the hands — washing the mouth in company is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes acceptable hand washing at table from unacceptable mouth rinsing in company.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102d. It is out of use to call upon the Company often to Eat nor need you Drink to others every Time you Drink
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unseemly and now almost out of fashion to frequently and importunately invite the company to eat; likewise, do not propose toasts to others every time you drink. If someone drinks to you, you may modestly decline or sip a little wine to be courteous, depending on company and custom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on frequency of invitations and toasts; offers polite refusal strategies and notes cultural sensitivity to refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: 103d. In Company of your Betters be not [longer in eating] than they are; lay not your Arm but ar[ise with only a touch on the edge of the table.]
rubrics_metrics.description: When dining with superiors, finish eating no later than they do; do not keep arms on the table — place hands only on the edge of the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes deference in pace and posture when in presence of social superiors.

rubrics_metrics.name: 104th. It belongs to y'e Chiefest in Company to unfold his Napkin and fall to Meat first, But he ought to begin in time & to Dispatch with Dexterity that y'e Slowest may have time allowed him
rubrics_metrics.description: The most distinguished person present should unfold his napkin and begin eating first; that person should, however, begin at a reasonable time and manage the meal so adroitly that slower diners have time to eat at their leisure — e.g., taste slowly, introduce light table-talk to allow others to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual duty: precedence in beginning, plus considerate pacing and hospitality to accommodate dilatory guests.

rubrics_metrics.name: 105th. Be not Angry at Table whatever happens & if you have reason to be so, Shew it not; put on a Chearfull Countenance especially if there be Strangers for good Humour makes one Dish of Meat a Feast
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not display anger at the table under any circumstance; even if you are justified in being angry, conceal it — particularly in the presence of strangers — and maintain a cheerful countenance, as good humor enhances a meal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social benefit: cheerfulness improves the communal dining experience; avoid creating embarrassment or discomfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: 106th. Set not yourself at y'e upper [end] of y'e Table but if it be your Due or that y'e Master of y'e house will have it so, Contend not least you Should Trouble y'e company
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not seat yourself at the head of the table voluntarily; if the seat rightfully belongs to you or the master of the house assigns it to you, accept without excessive refusal so as not to annoy the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises modesty about claiming honors but also cautions against performative refusal that disturbs others.

rubrics_metrics.name: 107th. If others talk at Table be attentive but talk not with Meat in your Mouth
rubrics_metrics.description: Be attentive when there is reading or conversation at table; if you must speak, do not do so with food in your mouth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates multiple earlier injunctions about not speaking with a full mouth and about attentiveness to table discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: 108th. When you Speak of God or his Attributes, let it be Seriously & [with words of] Reverence. Honour & obey your Natural Parents altho they be Poor
rubrics_metrics.description: Speak seriously and reverently when speaking of God or divine matters; honor and obey your natural parents even if they are poor, since earthly parents may not give riches but spiritual promises remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains both religious speech etiquette and a moral duty to respect parents regardless of their material status.

rubrics_metrics.name: 109th. Let your Recreations be Manfull not Sinfull
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose recreations that are manly/uplifting rather than sinful; avoid taking pleasure in baiting beasts or spectacles of cruelty, as that is to glory in shameful acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cautions against cruel entertainments (e.g., baiting beasts) and encourages virtuous leisure activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 110th. Labour to keep alive in your Breast that Little Spark of Celestial fire called Conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to keep your conscience alive and active; conscience punishes the wicked and is a perpetual feast to the good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral exhortation: conscience is likened to celestial fire that must be maintained; foundational ethical principle underlying all other rules.
